Names and compatibility

Current GateFox names and the compatibility identities used by existing installations and saved chats.

About 4 min read · 4 sections

On this page
01 Current names 02 Existing installations 03 Explicit path migration 04 Saved chats

GateFox is the current product name. Harness Gateway and Subscription Gateway remain in some stored identities that installed services and saved chats use. These identities remain supported so naming changes preserve chats and permissions.

Current names

Surface Name
App GateFox.app
Commands gatefox, gateway and harness-gateway run the same gateway
Stable release tag vVERSION
App download GateFox-VERSION-macos-arm64.zip
CLI download gatefox-VERSION-macos-arm64.tar.gz
New gateway chat provider gatefox

See releasing for publication and app updates for signed installation and rollback.

Existing installations

Fresh installations use ~/.local/share/gatefox and, on macOS, ~/Library/Application Support/GateFox/gateway.json. An existing installation can retain ~/.local/share/subscription-gateway and ~/Library/Application Support/Subscription Gateway/gateway.json; updates keep using those locations. The explicit path migration below gives them canonical GateFox entry paths while retaining their original storage and ownership identity. Updates never apply this migration automatically. See the Mac app for configuration discovery.

Explicit path migration

gatefox migrate --json                  # Read-only preview, including blockers.
gatefox migrate --apply --json          # Only during a coordinated maintenance window.
gatefox migrate --revert --json         # Preview rollback.
gatefox migrate --apply --revert --json # Remove only aliases this transaction created.

Install the matching GateFox app and CLI before applying this migration. Close ChatGPT and GateFox and stop the managed service deliberately with the operator; the command never closes an app, unloads a job, restarts a process or starts a service. Loaded jobs, active writers, installer locks and pending app updates block application. A preview reports these blockers without writing files.

For an existing installation, migration creates these verified aliases:

Canonical entry Original storage retained
~/Library/Application Support/GateFox ~/Library/Application Support/Subscription Gateway
~/.local/share/gatefox ~/.local/share/subscription-gateway

On Linux, the configuration entry is ~/.config/gatefox, backed by ~/.config/subscription-gateway. Fresh canonical installations need no alias. Independent directories at both names are a conflict; migration never merges or overwrites them. Foreign links, writable backing folders and unowned files are refused.

The backing folders deliberately keep their existing names. Moving them would invalidate absolute paths held by immutable releases, updater rollback and older service registrations. GateFox's command, installer and native app recognize only the exact owned alias and continue using the original configuration identity. Relative credential paths, executor ownership hashes and app preferences therefore stay the same. There is one data store, one installation and one background job.

A private receipt at ~/.local/state/gatefox-rename/transaction.json records the aliases and their filesystem identities. Retrying resumes recorded publications; rollback removes only the recorded links after checking every one. It keeps data, permissions and the receipt. Preexisting aliases are never adopted for rollback. Applying again after rollback archives the reverted receipt before starting a new transaction. If a process dies between creating a link and recording its inode, retry refuses to claim that uncertain link; preserve the receipt and review that link before recovery. A replaced or missing recorded link also requires review. Do not delete backing storage to resolve a rename conflict.

To return to an older app/CLI release, revert these aliases with the matching migration-capable release first, then follow the normal release rollback. Historical releases do not understand the canonical aliases' ownership contract.

The following identities must not be removed as cosmetic cleanup:

Identity Why it remains
com.edihasaj.subscription-gateway* LaunchAgent labels and ownership markers They identify existing managed services and recovery records. They remain compatibility keys; the signed app supplies the GateFox name and icon.
com.edihasaj.harness-gateway.app bundle ID Keeping it preserves the app's signing identity, permissions and background association.
HARNESS_GATEWAY_EXECUTOR alongside GATEFOX_EXECUTOR Running executors and SDKs may read either marker.
Symbol.for("harness-gateway/…") registry keys Loaded releases share live sessions and ownership through these keys.
A Harness Gateway.app compatibility link A loaded service can still refer to that path until its next natural start.

App relocation accepts only the verified sibling app relationship described in app updates. It does not authorize changing arbitrary app paths or macOS privacy records.

Saved chats

Current gateway executors register both gatefox and subscription_gateway. Existing chats keep opening under their recorded provider ID; migration is optional. A resume never rewrites a chat's provider identity.

gatefox chats migrate previews a supported saved-chat migration; --revert previews the reverse direction. To make changes, quit ChatGPT and stop the gateway service normally, then use --apply or --apply --revert. The command requires the canonical provider registration, backs up the database, and preserves native chats. It updates rollout metadata before database rows so an interrupted migration can be resumed. Keep the generated backups.

This is separate from path migration, which never rewrites chats. The saved-chat command's reverse direction selects every gatefox chat, including chats originally created with that identity; it is not transaction-specific rollback. Keep saved provider identities in place when preserving those existing GateFox chats matters. Both provider IDs remain supported.

See harness identity for the full saved-chat contract.
